JUDGMENT:
1.

This Judgment shall decide the present appeal filed by the appellant No.1 company and other individual working in it viz. appellant Nos. 2 to 4 under Section 76 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 as amended upto date (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing impugned order dated 02.06.2021 passed by the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (District East), Delhi,
whereby the appellant have been convicted under Section 23(1), 26(1), 26(2)(ii), 27(1), 27(2)(c),
27(3)(c) read with Section 3(1)(zF) (C)(i) of the FSS Act and also for violation of Regulation No.
2.2.1.5, 2.2.1.7 and 2.2.210 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter referred as FSS (P&L) Regulations) besides the importer respondent no. 6 for being found in violation of Section 25(1) (i) of FSS Act and thereby each of the individual appellant Nos. 2 and 4 have been sentenced to pay penalty of Rs. 10,000/ whereas appellant No. 3 has been sentenced to pay find of Rs. 20,000/, while the appellant No.1 company has been imposed with fine of Rs.30,000/ as also Sh. Abhishek Jain and M/s. Topnotch Retail Pvt. Ltd., respondent no. 5 & 6 respectively who have been imposed with fine of Rs.30,000/ each with directions to pay the penalty amount within 15 days of the order.

BRIEF FACTS:
2. Briefly stated, the appeal was filed on 15.07.2021 and it is within the period of limitation as prescribed in Rule 3.3.1 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.

The case as brought out in the appeal is that appellant No.4 Bipin Kumar Maurya is the FBO/Assistant Restaurant Manager in one of the outlet of Pizza Hut (Devyani International Ltd.) situated at G48, V3S Mall, Plot No.10,
District Central, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi110096; and that the appellant No.2 Sh. Pradeep Kumar is the nominee of the said outlet whereas appellant No.3 Arun Kumar is the nominee of the Warehouse of the company situated at W111, Gurgaon Dry Warehouse, Plot No. 18, Sector35, Gurugaon122004 whereas appellant No.1 M/s. Devyani International Ltd. is a company duly incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 having its corporate office at Plot No.18, Sector3, Gurugram, Haryana.

It is stated that the appellant No.1 is engaged in the 'Food & Beverages Industry' and holds impeccable reputation for its tinge free track records having more than 500 outlets in various parts of India.

3. It is stated that on 21.06.2018 at about 3.30 p.m. the complainant Ms. Anjali, Food Safety Officer (FSO) inspected the store of appellant No.1 company after disclosing her identity to FBO/ Vendor i.e., the appellant No.4 and she purchased "Fusilli Barilli (Pasta)" i.e., a sampled commodity on payment of Rs. 360/ towards the cost of the sample vide credit notice receipt dated 21.06.2018,
which consisted for 4X500 gms of "Fusilli Barilli (Pasta)"
taken in the original sealed condition of the same batch having identical main label declaration; and that sample commodity were divided in four equal parts and sealed as per law.

To cut the long story short, after conducting the proceedings at the spot,
one counter part of the sample was forwarded to the Food Analyst, Delhi for analysis,

because there is violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1.5, 2.2.1.7 and 2.2.2.(10) of the FSS(P & L)
Regulations.

State of Himachal Pradesh, decided on 26.04.2017; and it is assailed on the ground that the Adjudicating Officer/ADM failed to appreciate that the appellants had purchased the sampled commodity from M/s.

DECISION:
6. I have given my anxious thought to the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the appellants as also the Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the respondent.

I have gone through the relevant record of the present appeal as also the record of the AO/ADM as also written submissions M/S. Devyani International Ltd vs State on 24 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25667495/

sentences.text: No written submissions are filed by the respondent.
7. At the outset, the impugned order dated 02.06.2021 passed by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM cannot be sustained in law.

First thing first, it would be expedient to have a look at the Form 'VA',
which is the prescribed notice to the Food Business Operator, the scanned copy of which is annexed as 'AnnexureA' to this Judgment.
8.

Well, the scanned copy of the aforesaid notice is fully legible in this Judgment and it can be certainly deciphered that it gives minute details of the food item including Code Number, also reflecting FSSAI License number, manufacturing date and also the best before date.

It would be bear repetition that scanned copy of the notice also reflects that sealed poly packets of the food item i.e.
"Fusilli Barilli (Pasta)" Brand Romero had been seized and it is remarked that "it was not meant for direct sale as such and the same is used in preparation of pasta items like Arabita, Mushroom Pasta etc."

Provided that the existing products of a unit shall comply with the requirement of this clause on and after the six months of commencement of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Amendment Regulations, 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2.2.2.10. Best Before and Use By Date (i) the month and year in capital letters upto, which the product is best for consumption, in the following manner, namely:--
"BEST BEFORE ....... MONTHS AND YEAR"
OR "BEST BEFORE .......... MONTHS FROM PACKAGING OR "BEST BEFORE.....MONTHS FROM MANUFACTURE 9.

On a careful perusal of the aforesaid Regulation visvis the notice vide Form VA, what is apparent is that if the notice was giving minute details of the labelling, how in the world an opinion was formed that it was a case of misbranding within the scope and ambit of Section 3 (zf) of the FSS Act.

What is clearly brought out from the original record of the Adjudicating Officer/ADM and the material brought on the record is that appellant Nos. 1 to 4 are the actual user or consumer of the food item and the record reflects that a notice was given to respondent No.6 in original complaint i.e. M/s. Topnotch Retail Pvt. Ltd. about the food item, which has been imported by it and respondent No.6 vide letter dated 30.10.2018 as also 24.12.2018 pointed out that the shipment of Romero Pasta has been imported from Spain, the sample of which had been cleared after appropriate lab analysis from FSSAI Central Office.

sentences.text: That being the case, there is substance in the plea raised by the learned Counsel for the appellants that no liability could have been fastened on them for the alleged misbranding of the product in terms of Section 26(4) of the FSS Act.

It is pertinent to mention that the term 'Food Business Operator' is defined by Section 3(o) of the FSS Act to mean 'any person by whom business is carried on or owned and is responsible for ensuring the compliance of this Act, Rules and Regulations made thereunder'.

Admittedly, the appellant Nos. 1 to 4 are not producer or manufacturer of the food item in question that has been purchased by them from respondent No.6 M/s. Topnotch Retail Pvt. Ltd. by virtue of invoices/bills, prepared in the ordinary course of business, which per se provides a valid defence to the appellants under Section 80(2) (d) (i) of the FSS Act that reads that "a defence may be raised that the person selling food item in the same condition as and when a person purchased it or sold the food in different condition".

But then the whole issue has to be seen from the perspective that admittedly the food item in question was not meant for direct sale for consumers in the Restaurant being run by the appellant Nos. 1 to 4.

There is no merit in the plea by the Ld. Chief PP for the respondent that it was a case of direct sale since the term 'sale' is defined by Section 3 (zr) of the FSS Act "to mean sale of any article of food, whether for cash or on credit or by way of exchange and whether by wholesale or retail for human consumption or use".
11.

To sum up, it was not a case of direct sale, and therefore, not covered by Section 26 and 27 of the FSS Act, and incidentally the latter provision is applicable only to "manufacturer, packer, whole seller, distributor and sellers".

At the cost of repetition, the food item was meant for consumption in the nature of preparation of certain recipes being offered by the appellant Nos. 1 to 4 to its consumers in retail business and it goes without saying that the appellants had no role with regard to label declaration on the food item.

It manifestly appears that the observation by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM is mechanical in nature simply relying on the report of the Food Analyst dated 04.07.2018, which is based on "no objective legal standards."
The impugned order passed by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM belies common sense and logic, and it appears to have been passed throwing all applicable legal norms to the wind.
Hence, the prosecution launched against the appellant Nos. 1 to 4 was unwarranted, bad in law and gross abuse of process of law.
12. In view of the foregoing reasons, the appeal filed by the appellant Nos. 1 to 4 is allowed and the impugned order dated 02.06.2021 passed by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM is set aside.
The original record of the Adjudicating Officer/ADM be sent back forthwith alongwith copy of this Judgment.
File of appeal be consigned to the Record Room.
